solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Where tapers are balanced unsteadily by artist

indicators.note: something placed unsteadily wobbles out of position, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: Candles are perched precariously, apparently arranged by some careless painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsteadily' rearranges BALANCED into CANDELAB; 'by' simply places RA beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A branched holder for several candles is exactly the place where slender tapers stand.

clue.text: Author Diana toured new home for workers

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the author's surname goes around the other letter

parts.note: Diana Athill was a British editor and memoirist

explanation.surface: A literary figure travels around somewhere unfamiliar.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana Athill (1917-2019) was a celebrated London editor and memoir writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants are the labouring caste of a colony, and their nest mound is where they live.

clue.text: Drank heavily going round warehouse

indicators.note: turning round makes the word read the other way, back to front

parts.note: to tope is an old word meaning to drink alcohol to excess

explanation.surface: Someone boozing their way around a storage building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns TOPED back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A storage building or yard for goods is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Publican shows hostility beside Poles in shelter

indicators.note: placed in means put within the letters of another word

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

indicators.note: beside places one piece directly next to the other

parts.note: ice suggests coldness or frostiness of manner
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A barman is unfriendly, standing next to some Polish people under cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles are the magnetic north and south, N and S, not people from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub landlord holds a licence to sell alcohol, so is the licence holder.

clue.text: I neglect offer to work in Times for church approval

indicators.note: placed in means put within the letters of another word

parts.note: in arithmetic, six times two is six by two

indicators.note: setting letters to work moves them around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone ignores a job offer at the Times newspaper to win the Church's blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not the newspaper but multiplication, as in six by two; 'to work' shuffles the thirteen letters of I NEGLECT OFFER.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the sanction or blessing of the church, as in marrying, or once clerics' exemption from secular courts.

clue.text: Presenter ran choral group

indicators.note: the wanted letters form a group sitting together inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A broadcaster led a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group' signals letters grouped inside 'ran choral'.
explanation.definitionFit: A news presenter who links a programme is called its anchor, chiefly in American usage.

clue.text: Conflict over East River

indicators.note: one word lying over another covers it, here enclosing the single letter

parts.note: war is armed conflict
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Fighting spreads beyond the eastern bank of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear flows through Durham and Sunderland in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of an English river in County Durham.

clue.text: Comic that costs £140 on board and is pink

definitions.meaning: Jack ... is a British stand-up comedian

definitions.text: that costs £140 on board and is pink
definitions.meaning: on the London Monopoly board, the pink set includes the street of government offices priced at £140

explanation.surface: A funny performer apparently has a price and a rosy colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' refers to the Monopoly board, whose London streets each have a price and colour group.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian's surname and a Monopoly property square share this name.

clue.text: Colourful style of a Republican Dail member and novelist

parts.note: a TD (Teachta Dala) is a member of the Dail, the Irish parliament
Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist

explanation.surface: An Irish politician and a writer share a vivid manner.
explanation.walkthrough: TD is the Irish equivalent of MP.
explanation.definitionFit: The decorative 1920s-30s design movement was known for bold geometry and bright colour.

clue.text: Stage favourites return

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: pets are favoured people, as in teacher's pets

explanation.surface: Popular performers come back to the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' looks like a theatre but means a phase or degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage in a process is one step along the way.

clue.text: They're called up to study texts

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
scripts are written texts

explanation.surface: Students or actors summoned to examine written material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called up' suggests being phoned, but means drafted into military service.
explanation.definitionFit: Drafted soldiers are summoned into compulsory service, the military sense of being called up.

clue.text: Dry Parisian well walls corroded

indicators.note: walls surround, so the French word encloses the abstemious letters

parts.note: bien is French for well
TT means teetotal, someone who stays off alcohol

explanation.surface: A dried-up well in Paris has eroded walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' is French here, as 'Parisian' signals; 'Dry' means abstaining from drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal eaten away by acid is said to be bitten, as in etching.

clue.text: Fully developed female let down

parts.note: to let something down is to lower it

explanation.surface: A grown woman feels disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let down' reads as disappointed, but means physically lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that has bloomed has reached maturity, figuratively anything that has blossomed fully.

clue.text: Articulate European crowd welcome heartless monarch

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one set of letters receives the other

parts.note: a lot is a group or crowd of people

indicators.note: losing the heart means dropping the central letter

parts.note: a queen is a female monarch

explanation.surface: A well-spoken European throng greets a cold-hearted ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle E from QUEEN to leave QUEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent and persuasive in speech, an adjectival sense matching articulate.

clue.text: Notice pig breaking fast briefly, using roots?

indicators.note: breaking into a word splits it open to admit other letters
briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: quick means fast
an ad is a notice or advertisement
pig and rat are both insults for a contemptible person

explanation.surface: An advert about a greedy person who stops dieting by eating root vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims QUICK to QUIC; 'breaking' puts ADRAT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Equations involving squares are solved by finding their square roots, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Longing to leave in a Golf

indicators.note: placed in means set within the letters of another word

parts.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone eager to depart in a Volkswagen car.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf is both a VW car and the radio code word for G.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagerly expectant, keen to see or hear something.

clue.text: Efficient English wag keeps working

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a wag is a joker or comic
on means operating or working

explanation.surface: An English joker goes on performing effectively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wag' is a joker, not a tail movement; 'keeps' signals holding the working letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Economical, wasting nothing, is a sense this word shares with efficient.

clue.text: A medic recalled last part of movement

indicators.note: called back means sent in reverse, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: doc is short for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor was summoned back for the final stage of a campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' is a musical section, not a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A concluding passage added to a musical piece closes it off.

clue.text: Risk inflation? Take hour out and risk it again?

indicators.note: take with out means remove, so a letter is extracted
with take, out signals the removal of a letter

parts.note: an economy that overheats risks rising prices

explanation.surface: Economic advice on cutting working hours to avoid repeating risky growth.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'risk it' means risking a swollen belly, the inflation of a gorging diner.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating too much risks bodily swelling, a jokey kind of inflation.

clue.text: Occupants of 28 do this renovation

definitions.meaning: people in a tall tower stand facing the elevator
a cosmetic refurbishment of a building, or cosmetic surgery

explanation.surface: Tower workers carry out a refurbishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: occupants of a tall building face the lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic smartening of a building borrows the term for surgery to tighten the skin.

clue.text: Delicate paper kept in folder

indicators.note: kept in means held inside another word

parts.note: a file is a folder for documents
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A fragile document is stored in a folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' means a newspaper, here a rag.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily broken, needing careful handling, synonymous with delicate.

clue.text: Press perhaps breaks down, missing hub

indicators.note: something that breaks down falls apart, so the letters are reassembled
the hub is the centre, so the middle letter of the seven is dropped

explanation.surface: A newspaper may suffer a collapse without its central office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing hub' drops the central H of PERHAPS, leaving PERAPS for 'breaks down' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The press means the newspapers collectively.

clue.text: Dance over here disturbed nightspot in Berlin

indicators.note: one word over another covers it, so the dance surrounds the rearranged letters

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: disturbed letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A dance moving over here upset a Berlin club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means covering: the dance surrounds the letters that 'disturbed' scrambles.
explanation.definitionFit: German taverns serving lager are a typical venue for a night out in Berlin.

clue.text: Workers collect this chest he's left in close

indicators.note: placed in means set within the letters of another word

parts.note: near means close by

indicators.note: left means gone away, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: the letters H, E and S are taken from the word

explanation.surface: Labourers gather this chest a man left in a cathedral close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' are worker bees; 'he's left' removes H, E, S from CHEST to leave CT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees gather this sweet fluid from flowers to make honey.

clue.text: Feature a service

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A clue so terse it reads as an advertisement for a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' is a set of dishes, not a favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner service is a set of porcelain plates and dishes.

clue.text: Skinhead cornered alcohol

parts.note: police kettle protesters by penning them in
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed thug, boxed in, turns to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' means an instrument with a skin head, not a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A timpani has a skin stretched across its top, so it is literally a skin head.

clue.text: One teacher backs flag

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: backs means goes backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: sir is what pupils call a male teacher

explanation.surface: A single teacher supports a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is a plant, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild species of this plant, so flag is an alternative name.

clue.text: Bar measure excluding priest involved with hearing

indicators.note: excluding means leaving out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: an optic is a pub device that measures out spirits

explanation.surface: A pub rule that bans clergy, considered at a legal hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: An optic is the upside-down bottle dispenser behind a British bar.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective relates to the ear, the organ of hearing.

clue.text: Broadcaster's bound to cover rare gherkin, say

parts.note: Sky is a British broadcaster

indicators.note: covering means enclosing, so the leap goes around the letter

parts.note: a caper is a playful bound or leap

explanation.surface: A TV company must report on an unusual pickle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gherkin is a London office tower, so 'gherkin' is not a pickle here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gherkin is a famous example of a very tall tower in the City of London.
